```{r Define Functions}
# Functions

spaghetti_plot <- function(data, title) {
  result <- data %>%
          filter(!is.na(value_cfdna)) %>%

          # Added color = as.factor(patient_id) to the aesthetics mapping
          ggplot(aes(x = assigned_month, y = value_cfdna, group = patient_id, color = as.factor(patient_id))) +

          # Removed the static color assignments from geom_line and geom_point
          geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
          geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 1.5) +

          geom_hline(yintercept = 1.0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.7) +

          theme_minimal() +
          labs(
                  title = paste0("Longitudinal dd-cfDNA Trajectories - ", title),
                  subtitle = "Each color represents a different patient. Red dashed line indicates 1.0% threshold.",
                  x = "Time (Months)",
                  y = "dd-cfDNA (%)"
          ) +

          scale_x_continuous(breaks = target_months) +
          # scale_y_continuous(trans='log2') +
          theme(
                  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
                  panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),

                  # CRITICAL: Hide the legend!
                  # If you have dozens or hundreds of patients, the legend will take up the whole screen.
                  legend.position = "none"
          )
  result
}


spaghetti_plot_categorical <- function(data, title) {
  result <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(value_cfdna)) %>%

    # Added color = as.factor(patient_id) to the aesthetics mapping
    ggplot(aes(x = assigned_month, y = positivity, group = patient_id, color = as.factor(patient_id))) +

    # Removed the static color assignments from geom_line and geom_point

    ) +

      legend.position = "none"
    )
  result
}


transition_intervals_calc <- function(data, keep_all_patients = FALSE) {
  result <- data %>%
    arrange(patient_id, cfdna_time) %>%
    group_by(patient_id) %>%
    summarise(
      # Find the time of the FIRST positive test (suppress warnings for patients with no positive tests)
      first_pos_time = suppressWarnings(min(cfdna_time[positivity == 1], na.rm = TRUE)),

      # Find the time of the LAST negative test strictly BEFORE that first positive test
      last_neg_time = suppressWarnings(max(0, cfdna_time[positivity == 0 & cfdna_time < first_pos_time], na.rm = TRUE)),
      
      # --- NEW: Tracks the very last recorded test timepoint for the patient ---
      last_cfdna_time = suppressWarnings(max(cfdna_time, na.rm = TRUE)),

      .groups = "drop"
    ) 
  
  print(result)
  print("Raw")
  print(nrow(result))
  
  # --- NEW: Conditional evaluation of the filter sequence based on your boolean flag ---
  if (!keep_all_patients) {
    print("Filter finite pos time")
    result <- result %>% filter(is.finite(first_pos_time))
    print(nrow(result))
    
    print("Filter last neg time")
    result <- result %>% filter(is.finite(last_neg_time))
  } else {
    print("Bypassing filters: Keeping all patients (converting Inf/-Inf markers to NA/NaN)")
    # Clean up the mathematical Inf/-Inf values that min/max generate on empty vectors
    # so they don't break downstream statistical modeling packages.
    result <- result %>%
      mutate(
        first_pos_time = if_else(is.finite(first_pos_time), first_pos_time, NaN),
        last_neg_time  = if_else(is.finite(last_neg_time), last_neg_time, NaN),
        last_cfdna_time = if_else(is.finite(last_cfdna_time), last_cfdna_time, NaN)
      )
  }
  print(nrow(result))
  
  return(result)
}

cfdna_positivity <- function(cfdna, persist_positivity = TRUE) {
  result <- cfdna %>%
    # 1. Sort by patient and date to ensure chronological order
    arrange(patient_id, cfdna_time) %>%
    
    # 2. Group by patient so we don't accidentally compare 
    # the first test of Patient B to the last test of Patient A
    group_by(patient_id) %>%
    
    # 3. Create the necessary variables
    mutate(
      # Fetch the previous measurement using lag()
      prev_dd_cfdna = lag(value_cfdna),
      
      # Calculate the relative increase
      relative_increase = (value_cfdna - prev_dd_cfdna) / prev_dd_cfdna,
      
      # Create the binary positivity variable (1 = positive, 0 = negative)
      positivity = case_when(
        is.na(value_cfdna) ~ NA_real_,
        value_cfdna >= 1.0 ~ 1,
        value_cfdna >= 0.5 & relative_increase >= 0.61 & !is.infinite(relative_increase) ~ 1,
        TRUE ~ 0
      )
    )
  
  # --- NEW LOGIC: Make positivity persistent if the parameter is TRUE ---
  if (persist_positivity) {
    result <- result %>%
      mutate(
        # cummax() calculates the rolling maximum. Once it sees a 1, it stays 1.
        # coalesce(positivity, 0) ensures NAs don't break the cummax calculation.
        positivity = if_else(cummax(coalesce(positivity, 0)) == 1, 1, positivity)
      )
  }
  
  # 4. Ungroup the data to prevent issues in future analyses
  result <- result %>%
    ungroup()
  
  return(result)
}

cfdna_positivity_scheduled <- function(cfdna, schedule = c(36)) {
  
  schedule <- sort(schedule)

  result <- cfdna %>%
    # 1. Sort chronologically per patient
    arrange(patient_id, cfdna_time) %>%
    
    # 2. Group by patient
    group_by(patient_id) %>%
    
    # 3. Calculate baseline positivity
    mutate(
      prev_dd_cfdna = lag(value_cfdna),
      relative_increase = (value_cfdna - prev_dd_cfdna) / prev_dd_cfdna,
      
      positivity = case_when(
        is.na(value_cfdna) ~ NA_real_,
        value_cfdna >= 1.0 & type_cfdna == 1 ~ 1,
        value_cfdna >= 0.5 & relative_increase >= 0.61 & !is.infinite(relative_increase) ~ 1,
        TRUE ~ 0
      )
    )

  # 4. Persistence with dynamic reset AFTER scheduled samples
  result <- result %>%
    mutate(
      # ADDED `left.open = TRUE`
      # This ensures exact milestone matches (e.g., 36) stay in the previous interval.
      # The interval only increments for values strictly greater than the milestone.
      sched_milestone = findInterval(assigned_month, schedule, left.open = TRUE),
      
      # Check if the milestone index changed compared to the previous sample.
      is_reset_point = sched_milestone != lag(sched_milestone, default = -1),
      
      # Create persistent block IDs: increments ONLY strictly after a scheduled milestone
      reset_block = cumsum(is_reset_point)
    ) %>%
    # Group by patient AND reset block
    group_by(patient_id, reset_block) %>%
    mutate(
      # Roll positivity forward across unscheduled/missed intervals,
      # resetting only when a sample enters a new block
      positivity = if_else(
        is.na(positivity), 
        NA_real_, 
        cummax(coalesce(positivity, 0))
      )
    ) %>%
    # Regroup back to patient level and clean up helper columns
    group_by(patient_id) %>%
    select(-sched_milestone, -is_reset_point, -reset_block)

  # 5. Clean up groups
  result <- result %>%
    ungroup() %>% 
    filter(!is.na(positivity))

  return(result)
}

filter_post_positivity <- function(data) {
  result <- data %>%
    # 1. Ensure the observations are strictly chronological per patient
    arrange(patient_id, cfdna_time) %>%
    group_by(patient_id) %>%
    
    # 2. Apply the drop logic using a lagging cumulative sum
    filter(
      # Calculate the running total of positive tests up to the PREVIOUS row.
      # coalesce() handles the first row's lag safely by turning NA into 0.
      coalesce(lag(cumsum(coalesce(positivity, 0))), 0) == 0
    ) %>%
    
    # 3. Always ungroup to protect downstream statistical modeling
    ungroup()
  
  return(result)
}
```

# Descriptional Analysis of cfDNA Trajectories
Cluster the longitudinal data to identify the most likely surveillance schedule, to confirm the data matches what the clinic had in their protocol.
```{r Cluster time points and confirm testing schedule}

######## Figure out how many visits and when these visits are clustered #######
k_values <- 6:20
valid_times <- cfdna %>%
  filter(!is.na(cfdna_time)) %>%
  pull(cfdna_time)

# Calculate the "Total Within Sum of Squares" (variance) for each K
variance_explained <- map_dbl(k_values, function(k) {
  model <- kmeans(valid_times, centers = k, nstart = 10)
  return(model$tot.withinss)
})

# Plot the Elbow Curve
tibble(K = k_values, Variance = variance_explained) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = K, y = Variance)) +
  geom_line(color = pirche_primary_one_colors[1], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = pirche_primary_one_colors[2], size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:20) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Elbow Method for Determining Number of Scheduled Visits",
    subtitle = "Look for the 'elbow' where the line starts to flatten out",
    x = "Number of Clusters (Scheduled Visits)",
    y = "Total Within-Cluster Variance"
  )


# 2. Run K-medoids clustering (essentially K-means but with medians - thus less susceptible for supergravity of outliers)
# set.seed ensures you get the exact same clusters every time you run the script
set.seed(42)
num_expected_visits <- 15
medoids <- pam(valid_times, k = num_expected_visits)

# 3. Extract the cluster centers (these are your data-driven schedule days)
data_driven_days <- sort(as.numeric(medoids$medoids))

chronological_order <- order(medoids$medoids)
ordered_test_counts <- medoids$size[chronological_order]

# 2. Rebuild the discovery table with the counts included
schedule_discovery <- tibble(
  Visit_Number = 1:num_expected_visits,
  Approx_Days = round(data_driven_days, 1),
  Approx_Months = round(data_driven_days / days_per_month, 1),

  # Add the number of data points (tests) per cluster
  Number_of_Tests = ordered_test_counts
)

tibble(Time = valid_times) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = Time)) +

  # 1. Plot the density of the actual testing days
  geom_density(
    fill = pirche_primary_two_colors[2],
    alpha = 0.4,       # Semi-transparent fill
    color = pirche_primary_two_colors[2], # Outline color
    adjust = 0.25
  ) +

  # 2. Add the vertical lines for the discovered clusters
  geom_vline(
    data = schedule_discovery,
    aes(xintercept = Approx_Days),
    color = pirche_primary_one_colors[1],
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.8  # Note: Use 'size' instead of 'linewidth' if using an older version of ggplot2
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    data = tibble(months = target_months * 30.4375),
    aes(xintercept = months),
    color = pirche_primary_one_colors[2],
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1.0
  ) +

  # 3. Clean up the aesthetics
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Density of cfDNA Test Times",
    subtitle = "Grey dashed lines indicate data-driven schedule points (K-Medoids Centers), purple dashed lines indicate manually defined testing",
    x = "Time of Test (Days)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  )

schedule_discovery
```

```{r Temporal Alignment}
# temporal adjustment
target_days <- target_months * days_per_month
cfdna_aligned <- cfdna_binary %>%
  mutate(
    # map_dbl iterates through every single cfdna_time value
    assigned_month = map_dbl(cfdna_time, ~ {
      # Handle missing values safely
      if (is.na(.x)) return(NA_real_)

      # Calculate the absolute difference between the actual test day and all target days
      distances <- abs(target_days - .x)

      # Find the index of the smallest distance
      closest_idx <- which.min(distances)

      # Return the corresponding month from our original target_months list
      target_months[closest_idx]
    })
  )

  # Keep only the cfDNA value with the value in case of duplicates per month
cfdna_aligned_unique <- cfdna_aligned %>%
  group_by(patient_id, assigned_month) %>%

  slice_max(order_by = value_cfdna, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%

  # 3. Ungroup the data for downstream analysis
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(
    select(core, patient_id, PIRCHE_II),
    by = "patient_id"
  )
```

```{r cfdna vendors}

# 1. Clean the data: Filter out Omnigraf and drop the empty factor level
plot_type_data <- cfdna_filtered %>%
  # Filter out the specific rows
  filter(type_cfdna != 4) %>%
  filter(!is.na(type_cfdna) & !is.na(value_cfdna)) %>%
  
  # Convert to factor AND explicitly drop unused levels
  mutate(type_cfdna = fct_drop(as_factor(type_cfdna)))

print(paste0("total tests:",  nrow(plot_type_data)))

type_fractions <- plot_type_data %>%
  # 1. Count the occurrences of each cfDNA type
  count(type_cfdna, name = "Count") %>%
  
  # 2. Calculate the raw fraction and format it as a readable percentage
  mutate(
    Fraction = Count / sum(Count),
    Percentage = scales::percent(Fraction, accuracy = 0.1) # e.g., 45.2%
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Sort from most common to least common
  arrange(desc(Fraction))

# Print the result to the console
print(type_fractions)


cfdna_raw_medians_by_type <- cfdna_filtered %>%
  # 1. Group by the cfDNA assay type
  group_by(type_cfdna) %>%
  
  # 2. Calculate the median and count the total samples
  summarise(
    Median_cfDNA = median(value_cfdna_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Samples = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Sort by the highest median first (optional)
  arrange(desc(Median_cfDNA))

# Print the result to the console
print(cfdna_raw_medians_by_type)

cfdna_medians_by_type <- cfdna_filtered %>%
  # 1. Group by the cfDNA assay type
  group_by(type_cfdna) %>%
  
  # 2. Calculate the median and count the total samples
  summarise(
    Median_cfDNA = median(value_cfdna, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Samples = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Sort by the highest median first (optional)
  arrange(desc(Median_cfDNA))

# Print the result to the console
print(cfdna_medians_by_type)

# 2. Calculate the statistical significance (Pairwise Wilcoxon Test)
# Now safely executes without empty level errors!
unique_vendors <- unique(plot_type_data$type_cfdna)
if (length(unique_vendors) >= 2) {
  # --- Standard execution if multiple groups exist ---
  stat_test <- plot_type_data %>%
    wilcox_test(value_cfdna ~ type_cfdna) %>%
    adjust_pvalue(method = "bonferroni") %>%
    add_significance()
    
} else {
  # --- Safety fallback if only 1 vendor type is present ---
  message("Only one cfDNA vendor type detected (", unique_vendors, "). Skipping Wilcoxon test.")
  
  # Create a placeholder dataframe with the exact same structure rstatix returns
  # so that your downstream plotting/printing functions don't break.
  stat_test <- tibble(
    .y. = "value_cfdna",
    group1 = unique_vendors,
    group2 = "None",
    n1 = nrow(plot_type_data),
    n2 = 0,
    statistic = NA_real_,
    p = NA_real_,
    p.adj = NA_real_,
    p.adj.signif = "ns"
  )
}

# 3. Calculate non-outlier upper whisker limit to set the zoom window safely
whisker_data <- plot_type_data %>%
  summarise(
    q3 = quantile(value_cfdna, 0.75),
    iqr = IQR(value_cfdna),
    upper_whisker = q3 + (1.5 * iqr)
  )
global_whisker_max <- max(whisker_data$upper_whisker)

# 4. Manually set the height for the significance brackets right above the whiskers
stat_test_enriched <- stat_test %>%
  mutate(
    y.position = global_whisker_max + (row_number() * 0.2)
  )

# 5. Generate the Boxplot with Significance Brackets
cfdna_value_boxplot <- ggplot(plot_type_data, aes(x = type_cfdna, y = value_cfdna, fill = type_cfdna)) +
  
  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.7,
    outlier.shape = NA, 
    width = 0.5
  ) +
  
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    stat_test_enriched, 
    label = "p.adj.signif", 
    tip.length = 0.001
  ) +
  
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, max(stat_test_enriched$y.position) * 1.1)) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of dd-cfDNA Values by Assay Type",
    subtitle = "Brackets indicate Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise Wilcoxon significance, outliers hidden",
    x = "Assay Platform Type",
    y = "dd-cfDNA (%)"
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = cfdna_vendors) +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "none", 
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1)
  )
print(cfdna_value_boxplot)

# 1. Clean data and calculate overall positivity rate per assay type

  # Filter out missing records and drop the Omnigraf level
```

```{r Time-dependent hit-rate}
low_pirche_label <- paste0("Low PIRCHE-T2 (<", pirche_cutoff, ")")
high_pirche_label <- paste0("High PIRCHE-T2 (≥", pirche_cutoff, ")")

cfdna_transient <- cfdna_positivity(cfdna_filtered, persist_positivity = FALSE)

# 1. Prepare the data: Calculate Ratio and Power, then filter out low-volume bars
plot_pirche_ratios <- cfdna_transient %>%
  filter(!is.na(positivity) & !is.na(PIRCHE_II)) %>%
  
  mutate(
    PIRCHE_Group = if_else(PIRCHE_II < pirche_cutoff, low_pirche_label, high_pirche_label)
  ) %>%
  
  group_by(assigned_month, PIRCHE_Group) %>%
  summarise(
    Ratio = sum(positivity == 1) / n(),
    Total_Tests = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # --- NEW: Only keep bars that meet your data point threshold ---
  filter(Total_Tests > 15)

plot_pirche_ratios$PIRCHE_Group <- factor(
  plot_pirche_ratios$PIRCHE_Group, 
  levels = c(low_pirche_label, high_pirche_label)
)

custom_palette <- setNames(
  c(pirche_green, pirche_purple), 
  c(low_pirche_label, high_pirche_label)
)

plot_pirche_ratios <- plot_pirche_ratios %>%
  group_by(assigned_month) %>%
  mutate(
    # If this row is the highest ratio for the month, push it UP (+0.04)
    # Otherwise, push it DOWN (-0.04)
    y_nudge = if_else(Ratio == max(Ratio) | Ratio < 0.01, 0.01, -0.02)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 2. Generate the Grouped Bar Plot
library(ggrepel)

positivity_ratio_plot <- ggplot(plot_pirche_ratios, aes(x = assigned_month, y = Ratio, color = PIRCHE_Group)) +
  
  geom_line(alpha = 0.85, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.85) + 
  
  geom_label_repel(
    aes(label = paste0("n = ", Total_Tests)),
    
    # 1. Feed the custom directional vector into nudge_y
    nudge_y = plot_pirche_ratios$y_nudge, 
    
    # 2. Lock vertical movement so ggrepel doesn't undo your nudges
    direction = "x",        
    
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE,
    segment.color = "gray80", # Optional: adds a faint line connecting text to the point
    segment.size = 0.3
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Transient ddcfDNA Positivity Ratio by PIRCHE-T2",
    x = "Time Post-Transplant (Months)",
    y = "Positivity Ratio",
    color = "Immunological Risk Group" 
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = target_months) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_palette) +
  
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
print(positivity_ratio_plot)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, "positivity_ratio.png"), plot = positivity_ratio_plot, dpi = dpi, width = 1.2*fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)
```

```{r x-fold increased hit rate}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Reshape the longitudinal data frame and strip out zero-positivity months safely
monthly_fold_changes <- plot_pirche_ratios %>%
  # Standardize labels to clean column suffixes for pivoting
  mutate(Risk_Type = if_else(grepl("Low", PIRCHE_Group), "Low_Ratio", "High_Ratio")) %>%
  select(assigned_month, Risk_Type, Ratio) %>%
  
  # FIX: Cleanly handle duplicates by taking the mean if multiple rows exist
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Risk_Type, 
    values_from = Ratio,
    values_fn = list(Ratio = mean) # Safely squashes list-cols into true doubles
  ) %>%
  
  # Exclude months lacking complete data or where either group hits 0%
  filter(!is.na(Low_Ratio) & !is.na(High_Ratio) & Low_Ratio > 0 & High_Ratio > 0) %>%
  
  # Calculate the month-specific fold change
  mutate(Fold_Increase = High_Ratio / Low_Ratio)

# 2. Extract aggregate descriptive statistics (Median & IQR) across non-zero months
aggregate_metrics <- monthly_fold_changes %>%
  summarise(
    Median_Fold    = median(Fold_Increase),
    IQR_Lower_25th = quantile(Fold_Increase, 0.25),
    IQR_Upper_75th = quantile(Fold_Increase, 0.75),
    Total_Months   = n()
  )

# 3. Output Month-by-Month breakdown to console
cat("\n=== Distribution low PIRCHE (ZERO-POINTS EXCLUDED) ===\n")
print(summary(monthly_fold_changes %>% pull(Low_Ratio)))

cat("\n=== Distribution high PIRCHE (ZERO-POINTS EXCLUDED) ===\n")
print(summary(monthly_fold_changes %>% pull(High_Ratio)))

cat("\n=== MONTHLY TRAJECTORY BREAKDOWN (ZERO-POINTS EXCLUDED) ===\n")
print(monthly_fold_changes %>% select(assigned_month, Low_Ratio, High_Ratio, Fold_Increase))

# 4. Output Summary Metrics to console
cat("\n=== AGGREGATE SUMMARY FOOTPRINT ===\n")
cat(paste0("Total Months Evaluated:   ", aggregate_metrics$Total_Months, "\n"))
cat(paste0("Median Fold Increase:     ", round(aggregate_metrics$Median_Fold, 2), "x\n"))
cat(paste0("IQR Fold Increase Range: [", round(aggregate_metrics$IQR_Lower_25th, 2), "x - ", round(aggregate_metrics$IQR_Upper_75th, 2), "x]\n"))
cat("====================================\n")
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

cfdna_transient <- cfdna_positivity(cfdna_filtered, persist_positivity = FALSE)

# 1. Calculate dynamic tertile boundaries based on unique baseline patient values
tertile_cuts <- cfdna_transient %>%
  filter(!is.na(PIRCHE_II)) %>%
  distinct(patient_id, PIRCHE_II) %>% # Ensure each patient contributes only once to the boundary calculations
  mutate(tertile_num = ntile(PIRCHE_II, 3)) %>%
  group_by(tertile_num) %>%
  summarise(min_val = min(PIRCHE_II), max_val = max(PIRCHE_II), .groups = "drop")

# 2. Build explicit labels using the calculated dynamic boundaries
t1_label <- paste0("Low PIRCHE-T2 [", tertile_cuts$min_val[1], "-", tertile_cuts$max_val[1], "]")
t2_label <- paste0("Int PIRCHE-T2 (", tertile_cuts$min_val[2], "-", tertile_cuts$max_val[2], "]")
t3_label <- paste0("High PIRCHE-T2 (", tertile_cuts$min_val[3], "-", tertile_cuts$max_val[3], "]")

all_groups <- c(t1_label, t2_label, t3_label)

# 3. Process the data into the 3-tier structure
plot_pirche_ratios <- cfdna_transient %>%
  filter(!is.na(positivity) & !is.na(PIRCHE_II)) %>%
  mutate(
    # Apply global ntile categorization
    tertile_rank = ntile(PIRCHE_II, 3),
    PIRCHE_Group = case_when(
      tertile_rank == 1 ~ t1_label,
      tertile_rank == 2 ~ t2_label,
      tertile_rank == 3 ~ t3_label
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(assigned_month, PIRCHE_Group) %>%
  summarise(
    Ratio = sum(positivity == 1) / n(),
    Total_Tests = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(Total_Tests > 15)

# Enforce explicit factor sorting for the legend
plot_pirche_ratios$PIRCHE_Group <- factor(plot_pirche_ratios$PIRCHE_Group, levels = all_groups)

# 4. Define an expanded 3-color palette (adding an intermediate color)
# If 'pirche_orange' or similar is defined, use it, otherwise a neutral gray/orange bridge works well
pirche_intermediate_color <- "#E69F00" 

custom_palette <- setNames(
  c(pirche_green, pirche_intermediate_color, pirche_purple), 
  all_groups
)

# 5. Generate the Grouped Bar Plot (3 groups per timepoint)
positivity_ratio_plot <- ggplot(plot_pirche_ratios, aes(x = assigned_month, y = Ratio, fill = PIRCHE_Group)) +
  
  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity", 
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.85), # Tweaked slightly to give 3 bars space to dodge
    width = 0.8, 
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0("n = ", Total_Tests),
      group = PIRCHE_Group 
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.85),
    hjust = -0.2,           
    vjust = 0.4,
    angle = 90,             
    size = 2.8,              # Sized down slightly so 3 stacked text elements fit cleanly
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray20"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Transient ddcfDNA Positivity Ratio by PIRCHE-T2 Tertiles",
    subtitle = "Cohort divided into three equal-sized baseline immunological risk segments.",
    x = "Time Post-Transplant (Months)",
    y = "Positivity Ratio",
    fill = "Immunological Risk Tertile"
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = target_months) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) + # Extra ceiling padding
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_palette) +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )

print(positivity_ratio_plot)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, "positivity_ratio_tertiles.png"), plot = positivity_ratio_plot, dpi = dpi, width = fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)
```

```{r Create random event onset date}

# 1. Extract the transition intervals from the longitudinal data
transition_intervals <- transition_intervals_calc(cfdna_filtered)

# 2. Generate the random event time within that specific window
# Setting a seed ensures you get the exact same random numbers if you run the script again
set.seed(4321)

transition_intervals <- transition_intervals %>%
  mutate(
    # runif() generates random uniform numbers. It accepts vectors for min and max.
    random_event_time = runif(n(), min = last_neg_time, max = first_pos_time)
  )

# 3. Merge the new 'random_event_time' back into the Core dataset
core_filtered <- core_filtered %>%
  left_join(
    # Select only the ID and the new random date column to avoid cluttering Core
    select(transition_intervals, patient_id, random_event_time),
    by = "patient_id"
  )

# plot the event distribution
ggplot(transition_intervals %>% filter(!is.nan(random_event_time))) +
  
  # Density of the Random Event Times
  geom_density(
    aes(x = random_event_time, fill = "Random Event Time"), 
    alpha = 0.5, color = pirche_ocean_green, adjust = 0.25
  ) +
  
  # Density of the First Positive Test (The upper bound)
  geom_density(
    aes(x = first_pos_time, fill = "First Positive Test"), 
    alpha = 0.5, color = pirche_plum, adjust = 0.25
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Random Event Time vs. First Positive Test",
    x = "Time (Days)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Metric"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Random Event Time" = pirche_summer_green, "First Positive Test" = pirche_cannon_pink)) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
cfdna_positivity_distribution <- ggplot(
  transition_intervals %>% filter(!is.nan(random_event_time)), 
  aes(x = random_event_time)
) +
  
  # 1. Year-long relative histogram for Random Event Times
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count))),
    binwidth = 365,
    fill = pirche_summer_green,
    color = "white",          # Clean white borders between years
    alpha = 0.7,
    boundary = 0              # Forces bins to start exactly at 0 (0-365, 365-730, etc.)
  ) +
  
  # 2. Dynamic Text Labels showing percentages on top of each bar
  stat_bin(
    aes(
      y = after_stat(count / sum(count)),
      label = paste0(round(after_stat(count / sum(count)) * 100, 1), "%")
    ),
    binwidth = 365,
    boundary = 0,
    geom = "text",
    vjust = -0.5,             # Pushes the text slightly above the top of the bar
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.5,
    color = "gray15"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Distribution of Simulated Event Onset Times",
    subtitle = "Each bucket represents one year, y-axis shows the fraction of total events",
    x = "Time Post-Transplant (Days)",
    y = "Fraction of Cohort Events"
  ) +
  
  # Set X-axis breaks to happen exactly at year markers (0, 365, 730, 1095...)
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, max(transition_intervals$random_event_time, na.rm = TRUE) + 365, by = 365),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "\n(Yr ", round(x / 365), ")")
  ) +
  
  # Format the Y-axis as clean percentages and add padding at top so labels don't cut off
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent, 
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()
  )

# Output and save targets
print(cfdna_positivity_distribution)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, supplement, "cfdna_positivity_time.png"), plot = cfdna_positivity_distribution, dpi = dpi, width = fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)

# 1. Calculate the number of distinct cfDNA types per patient
patient_type_variability <- cfdna_filtered %>%
  filter(!is.na(type_cfdna)) %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  summarise(
    distinct_types = n_distinct(type_cfdna),

library(tidyverse)

# 1. Calculate patient-level sorting metrics
patient_order_metrics <- cfdna_filtered %>%
  filter(!is.na(type_cfdna)) %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  summarise(
    # Convert factor/labels to numeric to calculate a sorting "average"
    avg_type = mean(as.numeric(type_cfdna), na.rm = TRUE),
    total_tests = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Join metrics back and reorder the patient factor levels

  filter(!is.na(type_cfdna)) %>%
  inner_join(patient_order_metrics, by = "patient_id") %>%
  # Arrange the data by our target hierarchy (descending for both)

  mutate(patient_id = fct_inorder(factor(patient_id)))
```

# Correlation of cfDNA with PIRCHE scores
Just another sanity check, to confirm we're still in line with previous analyses of the Utah cohort.
```{r Correlation of cfDNA and PIRCHE-T2}

core_horizontal <- core_filtered %>%
        # 1. Create the grouping variable (same as before)
        mutate(
                transition_group = if_else(
                        patient_id %in% (transition_intervals %>% filter(!is.nan(random_event_time)) %>% pull(patient_id)),
                        "Has Transition",  # Shortened slightly to fit better on the axis
                        "No Transition"
                )
        ) %>%

        # 2. Reshape the data from wide to long format
        # This creates two new columns: 'PIRCHE_Type' and 'Score'
        pivot_longer(
                cols = c(PIRCHE_II, PIRCHE_II_A, PIRCHE_II_B, PIRCHE_II_C, PIRCHE_II_DRB1, PIRCHE_II_DQB1, PIRCHE_II_ClassII),
                names_to = "PIRCHE_Type",
                values_to = "Score"
        ) %>%

        # Remove missing scores to avoid ggplot warnings
        filter(!is.na(Score))

      core_horizontal %>%

        # 3. Build the base boxplot
        ggplot(aes(x = transition_group, y = Score, fill = transition_group)) +
        geom_boxplot(
                alpha = 0.7,
                outlier.colour = "red",
                outlier.alpha = 0.5
        ) +

        # 4. Facet the plot into 6 distinct panels based on the PIRCHE_Type
        facet_wrap(~ PIRCHE_Type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4, nrow=2) +

        # 5. Add the p-value calculation to every individual facet
        stat_compare_means(
                method = "wilcox.test",
                label = "p.format",
                vjust = -0.5
        ) +

        # Expand the Y-axis slightly so the p-values don't get cut off by the top border
        scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
        scale_fill_manual(values=rev(pirche_primary_one_colors)) +
        # 6. Formatting and themes
        theme_minimal() +
        labs(
                title = "PIRCHE Sub-scores by cfDNA Transition Status",
                x = NULL, # Hide the X-axis title since the labels are self-explanatory
                y = "Calculated Score"
        ) +
        theme(
```

```{r Kaplan Meier raw data}
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# 1. Calculate clinical event times for the full strategy
transition_intervals_full <- transition_intervals_calc(cfdna_filtered, keep_all_patients = TRUE)

all_groups <- c(low_pirche_label, high_pirche_label)

# 2. Enrich the event data with the baseline PIRCHE scores
km_data <- transition_intervals_full %>%
  left_join(
    core_filtered %>% select(patient_id, PIRCHE_II), 
    by = "patient_id"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(PIRCHE_II)) %>%
  
  # --- REVERTED: Binary risk stratification ---
  mutate(
    Risk_Group = if_else(PIRCHE_II < pirche_cutoff, low_pirche_label, high_pirche_label),
    
    # Define Survival Metrics
    Time_to_Event = if_else(!is.nan(first_pos_time), first_pos_time / days_per_month, observation_time / days_per_month),
    Event_Status  = if_else(!is.nan(first_pos_time), 1, 0)
  )

# Enforce clean factor ordering for the plot legend
km_data$Risk_Group <- factor(km_data$Risk_Group, levels = all_groups)

# 3. Fit the Kaplan-Meier Survival Model
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(Time_to_Event, Event_Status) ~ Risk_Group, data = km_data)

# 4. Generate the Kaplan-Meier Plot with Risk Table
km_plot <- ggsurvplot(
  km_fit,
  data = km_data,
  palette = c(pirche_green, pirche_purple), 
  
  # Keeps the active risk table fixes intact
  risk.table = TRUE,                         
  
  pval = TRUE,                               
  pval.method = TRUE,
  #log.rank.weights = "n",                    # "n" weights by the number of subjects at risk (Gehan-Breslow style)
  conf.int = TRUE,                           
  xlim = c(0, observation_time / days_per_month),                          
  break.time.by = 3,                        
  
  # Titles and Label Formatting
  title = "Time to de novo ddcfDNA Positivity by PIRCHE-T2",
  #subtitle = paste0("Stratified by PIRCHE-T2"),
  xlab = "Months Post-Transplant",
  ylab = "Probability of Remaining Transition-Free",
  legend.title = "Risk Cohort",
  legend.labs = all_groups,
  
  # Clean Aesthetics
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  tables.theme = theme_cleantable()
)

# Render the combined plot and risk table grid together
print(km_plot)
res <- arrange_ggsurvplots(list(km_plot), print = FALSE, ncol = 1, nrow = 1)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, "km_baseline.png"), plot = res, dpi = dpi, width = fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)

# 1. Extract the Kaplan-Meier summary specifically at month 36
km_summary_3yr <- summary(km_fit, times = 36)

# 2. Build a clean dataframe showing the cumulative incidence per group
incidence_3yr_table <- tibble(
  Risk_Group = gsub("Risk_Group=", "", km_summary_3yr$strata),
  Survival_Prob = km_summary_3yr$surv,
  
  # Cumulative Incidence = 1 - Survival
  Incidence_Raw = 1 - Survival_Prob,
  Incidence_Pct = scales::percent(Incidence_Raw, accuracy = 0.1),
  
  # Confidence Intervals for the incidence
  Lower_CI = scales::percent(1 - km_summary_3yr$upper, accuracy = 0.1), # Note upper/lower invert when subtracting from 1
  Upper_CI = scales::percent(1 - km_summary_3yr$lower, accuracy = 0.1)
)

# 3. Print the results cleanly to your console
cat("\n=== Cumulative Incidence at 3 Years (36 Months) ===\n")
print(incidence_3yr_table)
```

# Temporal alignment and emulated longitudinal trajectories
In order to horizontally line up the samples by date, we apply time-binning by finding the closest target month considering the absolute time difference between sample date and any of the scheduled time points.

## Continuous cfDNA value
```{r Thinning}
############################# create emulated reduced trajectories ###################################

# 2. Filter to keep ONLY tests that were mapped to the reduced schedule or are last in sequence
cfdna_thinned <- cfdna_filtered %>%
  # Group by patient to evaluate the "last sample" on an individual basis
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  
  # Keep the row if it's in the reduced schedule OR if it's the max month for this patient
  filter(
    (assigned_month %in% reduced_months) 
    #| 
    #(assigned_month == max(assigned_month, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

cfdna_personalized <- bind_rows(cfdna_filtered %>% filter(PIRCHE_II >= pirche_cutoff), cfdna_thinned %>% filter(PIRCHE_II < pirche_cutoff))

# 1. Extract the transition intervals from the longitudinal data
transition_intervals_thinned <- transition_intervals_calc(cfdna_thinned)
transition_intervals_personalized <- transition_intervals_calc(cfdna_personalized)


################### longitudinal time-warped cfDNA trajectories ###########################
longitudinal_full <- spaghetti_plot(cfdna_filtered, "High Frequency")
longitudinal_personalized <- spaghetti_plot(cfdna_personalized, "Personalized Frequency")
longitudinal_thinned <- spaghetti_plot(cfdna_thinned, "Low Frequency")
print(longitudinal_full)
print(longitudinal_personalized)
print(longitudinal_thinned)
```

## Categorical cfDNA based on positivity rules
Converting cfDNA trajectories here to binary as a sanity check. We need to consider treatment bias (i.e. "because a cfDNA was high, clinicians started treatment, which reduced cfDNA levels in the next sample")! As such, when thinning the tests, we may miss the transient positive cfDNA test. To account for that, we model in the original data, that once a cfDNA becomes positive, all subsequent tests are also positive. This doesn't hurt our feelings, as our observed variable is time-to-(first)-detection. As such, we expect here only low-to-high transitions (i.e. diagonals from bottom left to top right), but no high-to-low transitions.

Could also consider to transition patients to high frequency arm, once they get positive (which would increase test numbers a bit, but adds complexity - in a real RCT, that would be realistic behavior though!?)

```{r Plot categorical cfDNA trajectories}
################### longitudinal time-warped cfDNA trajectories ###########################

longitudinal_personalized_categorical <- spaghetti_plot_categorical(cfdna_personalized, "Personalized Frequency")
longitudinal_thinned_categorical <- spaghetti_plot_categorical(cfdna_thinned, "Low Frequency")
print(longitudinal_full_categorical)
print(longitudinal_personalized_categorical)
print(longitudinal_thinned_categorical)
```

Depending on PIRCHE cutoffs, more patients are put into high or low risk groups and monitored accordingly. We want to find a sweet spot here. Testing a couple interesting points (PIRCHE quartiles, and 100, just for the sake of it). Given our onset date of rejection is simulated, we repeat the process with different random initialization. 

Baselines are one-size-fits-all frequent and infrequent monitoring. Additionally, we emulate a 50%-powered random control arm in the study that gets infrequent cfDNA testing as a reference (black symbols).

```{r Simulate Cutoffs and Random Seeds}
# 1. Define simulation parameters

pirche_cutoffs <- c(23, 45, 50, 69)
random_seeds <- 1:1000
patient_level_results_list <- list() # Extracted container for downstream processing

# 2. Prepare the static baseline and thinned intervals
base_intervals <- transition_intervals

df_thin <- transition_intervals_thinned %>%
  select(patient_id, first_pos_time.thin = first_pos_time)

# extract cases with positivity event
emulation_cfdna_filtered <- cfdna_filtered
emulation_cfdna_thinned <- cfdna_thinned

# Calculate the absolute min and max testing burden globally
n_tests_full <- nrow(emulation_cfdna_filtered)
n_tests_thin <- nrow(emulation_cfdna_thinned)
rel_tests_full <- (n_tests_full / n_tests_thin) * 100
rel_tests_thin <- 100

# Pre-calculate the exact number of tests PER PATIENT across the ENTIRE cohort
patient_test_counts <- emulation_cfdna_filtered %>%
  count(patient_id, name = "n_full") %>%
  left_join(
    emulation_cfdna_thinned %>% count(patient_id, name = "n_thin"),
    by = "patient_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(n_thin = coalesce(n_thin, 0))

# Get the list of ALL unique patients for the control group coin-toss
all_patients <- patient_test_counts$patient_id

# Pre-calculate personalized configurations to save processing time
pers_configs <- list()
for (cutoff in pirche_cutoffs) {
  cfdna_pers <- bind_rows(emulation_cfdna_filtered %>% filter(PIRCHE_II >= cutoff), emulation_cfdna_thinned %>% filter(PIRCHE_II < cutoff))

  intervals_pers <- transition_intervals_calc(cfdna_pers) %>%
    select(patient_id, first_pos_time.pers = first_pos_time)

  n_tests_pers <- nrow(cfdna_pers)

  pers_configs[[as.character(cutoff)]] <- list(
    intervals = intervals_pers,
    n_tests = n_tests_pers,
    rel_tests = (n_tests_pers / n_tests_thin) * 100
  )
}

sim_results_list <- list()

# 3. Run the simulation across seeds
for (s in random_seeds) {
  set.seed(s)
  seed_patient_rows <- list()
  # A. Generate the random event times for this seed
  current_base <- base_intervals %>%
    mutate(random_event_time = runif(n(), min = last_neg_time, max = first_pos_time)) %>%
    select(patient_id, random_event_time, first_pos_time.full = first_pos_time)

  # Calculate TTD for both Baselines
  merged_base <- current_base %>%
    inner_join(df_thin, by = "patient_id") %>%
    mutate(
      ttd_full = first_pos_time.full - random_event_time,
      ttd_thin = first_pos_time.thin - random_event_time
    ) %>%
    filter(ttd_thin >= 0, ttd_full >= 0)

  med_full <- mean(merged_base$ttd_full, na.rm = TRUE)
  med_thin <- mean(merged_base$ttd_thin, na.rm = TRUE)

  rel_delay_full <- (med_full / med_thin) * 100
  rel_delay_thin <- 100

  # Store High Frequency Simulation (Both Relative and Absolute)
  sim_results_list[[length(sim_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
    Strategy = "EF",
    Seed = s,
    Relative_Tests = rel_tests_full,
    Relative_Delay = rel_delay_full,
    Absolute_Tests = n_tests_full,
    Absolute_Delay = med_full,
    n = nrow(merged_base)
  )
  # Append EF Patient-Level Data
  seed_patient_rows[[length(seed_patient_rows) + 1]] <- merged_base %>%
    select(patient_id, random_event_time, TTD = ttd_full) %>%
    mutate(Strategy = "EF", Seed = s)

  # Store Low Frequency Simulation (Both Relative and Absolute)
  sim_results_list[[length(sim_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
    Strategy = "SF",
    Seed = s,
    Relative_Tests = rel_tests_thin,
    Relative_Delay = rel_delay_thin,
    Absolute_Tests = n_tests_thin,
    Absolute_Delay = med_thin,
    n = nrow(merged_base)
  )
  
  # Append SF Patient-Level Data
  seed_patient_rows[[length(seed_patient_rows) + 1]] <- merged_base %>%
    select(patient_id, random_event_time, TTD = ttd_thin) %>%
    mutate(Strategy = "SF", Seed = s)

  # B. Calculate Random 1:2 Control Strategy
  high_freq_patients <- sample(all_patients, size = floor(2/3.*length(all_patients)))

  tests_control <- sum(patient_test_counts$n_full[patient_test_counts$patient_id %in% high_freq_patients]) +
    sum(patient_test_counts$n_thin[patient_test_counts$patient_id %in% all_patients & !(patient_test_counts$patient_id %in% high_freq_patients)])

  rel_tests_control <- (tests_control / n_tests_thin) * 100

  merged_control <- merged_base %>%
    mutate(
      ttd_control = if_else(patient_id %in% high_freq_patients, ttd_full, ttd_thin)
    )

  med_control <- mean(merged_control$ttd_control, na.rm = TRUE)
  rel_delay_control <- (med_control / med_thin) * 100

  sim_results_list[[length(sim_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
    Strategy = "RC 1:2",
    Seed = s,
    Relative_Tests = rel_tests_control,
    Relative_Delay = rel_delay_control,
    Absolute_Tests = tests_control,
    Absolute_Delay = med_control,
    n = nrow(merged_control)
  )
  
  # Append RC Patient-Level Data
  seed_patient_rows[[length(seed_patient_rows) + 1]] <- merged_control %>%
    select(patient_id, random_event_time, TTD = ttd_control) %>%
    mutate(Strategy = "RC 1:2", Seed = s)

  # C. Calculate Personalized TTDs for each cutoff
  for (cutoff in pirche_cutoffs) {
    config <- pers_configs[[as.character(cutoff)]]

    merged_pers <- merged_base %>%
      inner_join(config$intervals, by = "patient_id") %>%
      mutate(ttd_pers = first_pos_time.pers - random_event_time) %>%
      filter(ttd_pers >= 0)

    med_pers <- mean(merged_pers$ttd_pers, na.rm = TRUE)
    rel_delay_pers <- (med_pers / med_thin) * 100

    sim_results_list[[length(sim_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
      Strategy = paste0("PF (T2 ≥ ", cutoff, ")"),
      Seed = s,
      Relative_Tests = config$rel_tests,
      Relative_Delay = rel_delay_pers,
      Absolute_Tests = config$n_tests,
      Absolute_Delay = med_pers,
      n = nrow(merged_pers)
    )
    
    # Append PF Patient-Level Data
    seed_patient_rows[[length(seed_patient_rows) + 1]] <- merged_pers %>%
      select(patient_id, random_event_time, TTD = ttd_pers) %>%
      mutate(Strategy = paste0("PF (T2 ≥ ", cutoff, ")"), Seed = s)
  }
  
  patient_level_results_list[[s]] <- bind_rows(seed_patient_rows)
}

sim_results <- bind_rows(sim_results_list)
patient_level_results <- bind_rows(patient_level_results_list)
```

```{r plot efficiency}
# 4. Calculate Medians AND Error Bounds (Interquartile Range) for Both
seed_level_summary <- sim_results %>%
  group_by(Strategy, Seed) %>%
  summarise(
    # Get the unique or average baseline score for this specific seed run
    Relative_Delay = mean(Relative_Delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    Relative_Tests = mean(Relative_Tests, na.rm = TRUE),
    Absolute_Delay = mean(Absolute_Delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    Absolute_Tests = mean(Absolute_Tests, na.rm = TRUE),
    n              = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --- ROUND 2: Squash across the Seeds ---
summary_results <- seed_level_summary %>%
  group_by(Strategy) %>%
  summarise(
    # Relative Summaries (Squashing the 1,000 seeds)
    Med_Rel_Delay  = median(Relative_Delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    Low_Rel_Delay  = quantile(Relative_Delay, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    High_Rel_Delay = quantile(Relative_Delay, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Med_Rel_Tests  = median(Relative_Tests, na.rm = TRUE),
    Low_Rel_Tests  = quantile(Relative_Tests, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    High_Rel_Tests = quantile(Relative_Tests, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Absolute Summaries (Squashing the 1,000 seeds)
    Med_Abs_Delay  = median(Absolute_Delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    Low_Abs_Delay  = quantile(Absolute_Delay, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    High_Abs_Delay = quantile(Absolute_Delay, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Med_Abs_Tests  = median(Absolute_Tests, na.rm = TRUE),
    Low_Abs_Tests  = quantile(Absolute_Tests, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    High_Abs_Tests = quantile(Absolute_Tests, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),

    # Expected patient cohort size across all iterations
    n = mean(n, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate slope and intercept for the RELATIVE infinite line
med_high_rel_x <- summary_results$Med_Rel_Delay[summary_results$Strategy == "EF"]
med_high_rel_y <- summary_results$Med_Rel_Tests[summary_results$Strategy == "EF"]
med_low_rel_x <- summary_results$Med_Rel_Delay[summary_results$Strategy == "SF"]
med_low_rel_y <- summary_results$Med_Rel_Tests[summary_results$Strategy == "SF"]

tradeoff_slope_rel <- (med_low_rel_y - med_high_rel_y) / (med_low_rel_x - med_high_rel_x)
tradeoff_intercept_rel <- med_high_rel_y - tradeoff_slope_rel * med_high_rel_x

# Calculate slope and intercept for the ABSOLUTE infinite line
med_high_abs_x <- summary_results$Med_Abs_Delay[summary_results$Strategy == "EF"]
med_high_abs_y <- summary_results$Med_Abs_Tests[summary_results$Strategy == "EF"]
med_low_abs_x <- summary_results$Med_Abs_Delay[summary_results$Strategy == "SF"]
med_low_abs_y <- summary_results$Med_Abs_Tests[summary_results$Strategy == "SF"]

med_n <- mean(summary_results$n)

tradeoff_slope_abs <- (med_low_abs_y - med_high_abs_y) / (med_low_abs_x - med_high_abs_x)
tradeoff_intercept_abs <- med_high_abs_y - tradeoff_slope_abs * med_high_abs_x

# 5. Define Strategy Styling
strategy_colors <- c(
  "PF (T2 ≥ 23)" = pirche_gradient_11[1],
  "PF (T2 ≥ 45)" = pirche_gradient_11[5],

)

)

desired_strategy_order <- c("SF", "EF", "RC 1:2", "PF (T2 ≥ 23)", "PF (T2 ≥ 45)", "PF (T2 ≥ 50)", "PF (T2 ≥ 69)")

tick_relative_y <- 4
tick_relative_x <- 1.5
tick_absolute_y <- 60
tick_absolute_x <- 1.5

summary_results_ordered <- summary_results %>%
  mutate(Strategy = factor(Strategy, levels = desired_strategy_order))

# 6a. Generate the RELATIVE Scatter Plot
plot_relative <- ggplot(summary_results, aes(x = Med_Rel_Delay, y = Med_Rel_Tests, color = Strategy, shape = Strategy)) +
  geom_abline(slope = tradeoff_slope_rel, intercept = tradeoff_intercept_rel, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgray", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = Low_Rel_Delay, xmax = High_Rel_Delay), alpha = 0.6, width=tick_relative_y, linewidth = 0.8, orientation = "y") +

# 6b. Generate the ABSOLUTE Scatter Plot
```

# Analysis of emulated trajectories
The number of cfDNA tests in the real and emulated schedules (assuming no loss of follow-up or study drop-outs).
```{r Derive time-to-detection}
#######################################################################################################################################

patient_level_results_selected <- patient_level_results %>%
  # Filter down to the strategies you want to keep
  filter(Strategy %in% c("EF", "SF", "PF (T2 ≥ 45)")) %>%
  
  # Rename the cutoff 50 strategy to just "PF"
  mutate(
    Strategy = as.character(Strategy),
    Strategy = if_else(Strategy == "PF (T2 ≥ 45)", "PF", Strategy),
    Strategy = factor(Strategy) # Re-encode as factor for downstream grouping/plotting
  ) %>% 
  group_by(patient_id, Strategy) %>% 
  summarise(
    TTD = mean(TTD),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

patient_level_wide <- patient_level_results_selected %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(patient_id),
    names_from = Strategy,
    # Pull both metrics into the horizontal expansion
    values_from = c(TTD),
    # Use a clean separator for the new column names (e.g., TTD_PF, TTD_SF)
    names_sep = "."
  )
```

By removing samples (i.e. changing the previous sample), positivity may be introduced based on relative increase. This can lead to new positivity that wasn't assumed during simulation of an event onset date. Consequently, we may introduce negative time-to-detection.
We remove this artifact by removing these cases from the analysis.
```{r Filter negative time-to-detection cases}
print(nrow(patient_level_wide %>% filter(SF < 0)))
print(patient_level_wide %>% filter(SF < 0), width=Inf)
patient_level_wide <- patient_level_wide %>%
  #filter(time_to_detection.thin >= 0)
  filter(is.na(SF) | SF >= 0)
```

Time-to-detection based on immune surveillance schema considering a fixed PIRCHE score cutoff in the personalized schema. Given this is a paired significance test (because we have virtual twins in each of the columns), the p value is pretty low - yet the effect size is what matters here.
```{r Plot time-to-detection distributions}
my_comparisons <- list(
  c("EF", "PF"),
  c("PF", "SF"),
  c("EF", "SF")
)

plot_data_temp <- patient_level_wide %>%
  # 1. Reshape the data: gather the two columns into a long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(EF, PF, SF),
    names_to = "Dataset_Version",
    values_to = "Time"
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Time)) %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%

  # filter to have only complete cases (for paired testing)
  filter(n() == 3) %>%

  # Ungroup and sort so rows perfectly align for the paired Wilcoxon test
  ungroup() 

plot_data <- plot_data_temp%>%
  group_by(patient_id, Dataset_Version) %>%
  summarise(
    Time = mean(Time),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ungroup %>%
  arrange(patient_id, Dataset_Version)

stat_test <- plot_data %>%
  wilcox_test(
    Time ~ Dataset_Version,
    paired = TRUE,
    comparisons = my_comparisons
  )

group_medians <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(Dataset_Version) %>%
  summarise(med = median(Time), .groups = "drop")

group_means <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(Dataset_Version) %>%
  summarise(mn = mean(Time), .groups = "drop")
stat_test_enriched <- stat_test %>%
  left_join(group_medians, by = c("group1" = "Dataset_Version")) %>%
  rename(med1 = med) %>%
  left_join(group_medians, by = c("group2" = "Dataset_Version")) %>%
  rename(med2 = med) %>%
  left_join(group_means, by = c("group1" = "Dataset_Version")) %>%
  rename(mn1 = mn) %>%
  left_join(group_means, by = c("group2" = "Dataset_Version")) %>%
  rename(mn2 = mn) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_median = round(med2, 1) - round(med1, 1),
    delta_mean = round(mn2, 1) - round(mn1, 1),
    
    # SPLIT LOGIC: Define the upper and lower text components separately
    label_p_value = paste0("p = ", p),
    label_deltas  = paste0("ΔM = ", round(delta_median, 1), " days\nΔμ = ", round(delta_mean, 1))
  ) %>%
  add_y_position(step.increase = 0.22)

# 2. Build the boxplot
ttd_boxplot <- ggplot(data = plot_data, aes(x = Dataset_Version, y = Time, fill = Dataset_Version)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.7,
    outlier.colour = "red",
    outlier.alpha = 0.5
  ) +

  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 24,
    size = 2.5,
    fill = "white",
    color = "gray20",
    stroke = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # LAYER 1: Draws the actual geometric brackets and places the P-value ABOVE it
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    stat_test_enriched,
    label = "label_p_value",
    tip.length = 0.02,
    vjust = -0.4,             # Positive vertical offset (shifts up)
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  
  # LAYER 2: Suppresses the bracket lines (tip.length = 0) and drops the deltas BELOW it
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    stat_test_enriched,
    label = "label_deltas",
    tip.length = 0,           # Eliminates duplicate prong rendering
    remove.bracket = TRUE,    # Disables drawing duplicate line geometry entirely
    vjust = 1.25,             # Negative vertical offset (shifts down)
    lineheight = 0.9          # Tightens line spacing for the sub-metrics
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("SF" = pirche_gradient_11[11], "EF" = pirche_gradient_11[1], "PF" = pirche_gradient_11[5])) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Time to Detection (TTD)",
    x = "schedule",
    y = "time-to-detection (days)"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )
print(ttd_boxplot)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, "ttd_boxplot.png"), plot = ttd_boxplot, dpi = dpi, width = fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)


# 2. Calculate the descriptive statistics (Median, 25th, and 75th percentiles)
cohort_metrics <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(Dataset_Version) %>%
  summarise(
    Median = median(Time),
    Mean = mean(Time),
    Q1_25th = quantile(Time, 0.25),
    Q3_75th = quantile(Time, 0.75),
    Total_Patients = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Arrange metrics in order: EF, PF, SF
  arrange(factor(Dataset_Version, levels = c("EF", "PF", "SF")))

# 3. Output a clean summary block to your R console
cat("\n=======================================================\n")
cat("      DESCRIPTIVE STATS: TIME TO DETECTION (DAYS)      \n")
cat("=======================================================\n")
print(cohort_metrics)
cat("=======================================================\n\n")

# 4. Generate pre-formatted copy-paste inline text blocks for your manuscript
cat("--- Manuscript Text Ready Formats ---\n")
invisible(apply(cohort_metrics, 1, function(row) {
  cat(paste0(
    row["Dataset_Version"], " Group: Median = ", round(as.numeric(row["Median"]), 1),
    " days (IQR: ", round(as.numeric(row["Q1_25th"]), 1), 
    " to ", round(as.numeric(row["Q3_75th"]), 1), " days) ",
    " mean = ", round(as.numeric(row["Mean"]), 1), "\n"
  ))
}))

# 3. Output a clean summary block to your R console
cat("\n=======================================================\n")
cat("      DESCRIPTIVE STATS: LONG DETECTION CASES      \n")
cat("=======================================================\n")

long_detection_counts <- plot_data %>%
  # 1. Filter for rows where time is greater than 100 days
  # (and ensure there are no NA values in the relevant columns)
  filter(Time > 42 & !is.na(Time) & !is.na(Dataset_Version)) %>%
  
  # 2. Group by the cfDNA assay type
  group_by(Dataset_Version) %>%
  
  # 3. Count the rows meeting the condition
  summarise(
    Data_Points_Beyond_Days = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 4. Sort from highest count to lowest
  arrange(desc(Data_Points_Beyond_Days))

# Print the result to your console
print(long_detection_counts)
cat("=======================================================\n\n")
```

```{r}
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_palette) +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
print(plot_pirche_ratio_PF)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, supplement, "positivity_ratio_pf.png"), plot = plot_pirche_ratio_PF, dpi = dpi, width = fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggrepel)
library(gridExtra)

# 1. Normalize the metrics to a 0-1 scale WITHIN each random seed safely
sim_results_processed <- sim_results %>%
  group_by(Seed) %>%
  mutate(
    # Min-Max Scaling calculated strictly within each strategy's group
    Delay_Scaled = (Absolute_Delay - min(Absolute_Delay, na.rm = TRUE)) / 
                   (max(Absolute_Delay, na.rm = TRUE) - min(Absolute_Delay, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    Tests_Scaled = (Absolute_Tests - min(Absolute_Tests, na.rm = TRUE)) / 
                   (max(Absolute_Tests, na.rm = TRUE) - min(Absolute_Tests, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # Calculate composite score on locally weighted inputs
    nxttd = 1- 0.5*(Delay_Scaled + Tests_Scaled)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% # CRITICAL: Ungroup so the subsequent sorting and Wilcox tests run across strategies
  
  # Reorder the Strategy factor by the new localized median descending
  mutate(Strategy = fct_reorder(Strategy, nxttd, .fun = median, .desc = FALSE))
# 2. Define your target comparison pairs explicitly
target_comparisons <- list(
  c("RC 1:2", "EF"),
  c("PF (T2 ≥ 45)", "RC 1:2")
)

# 3. Compute Wilcoxon tests using highly resilient Base R wilcox.test()
compute_base_wilcox <- function(data, pair) {
  g1 <- data %>% filter(Strategy == pair[1]) %>% pull(nxttd)
  g2 <- data %>% filter(Strategy == pair[2]) %>% pull(nxttd)
  
  # Base R safely catches zero variance cases
  p_val <- tryCatch({
    wilcox.test(g1, g2, exact = FALSE, correct = TRUE)$p.value
  }, error = function(e) {
    return(1.0) # Safety fallback if vectors are completely uncomputable
  })
  
  tibble(
    group1 = pair[1],
    group2 = pair[2],
    p = if_else(is.na(p_val), 1.0, p_val)
  )
}

# Run the tests and apply the Bonferroni adjustment manually
selected_comparisons_raw <- map_dfr(target_comparisons, ~compute_base_wilcox(sim_results_processed, .x))

selected_comparisons <- selected_comparisons_raw %>%
  mutate(
    .y. = "nxttd",
    p.adj = pmin(p * length(target_comparisons), 1.0), # Bonferroni adjustment multiplier
    p.adj.signif = case_when(
      p.adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.adj < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.adj < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE          ~ "ns"
    )
  )

# 4. Map the geometric Y coordinates manually to avoid rstatix dependencies
# Find the absolute peak of your data to set the first bracket position
max_y <- max(sim_results_processed$nxttd, na.rm = TRUE)
y_step <- max_y * 0.12

selected_comparisons <- selected_comparisons %>%
  mutate(
    y.position = max_y + (row_number() * y_step),
    xmin = group1,
    xmax = group2
  )

# 5. Generate the sorted boxplot
nttd_plot <- ggplot(sim_results_processed, aes(x = Strategy, y = nxttd, color=Strategy, fill = Strategy)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 1.5) +
  
  # Overlay the manually generated robust brackets
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    selected_comparisons, 
    label = "p.adj.signif", 
    tip.length = 0.02
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "strategy",
    y = "efficiency\nMNT = (1 - mean(n, ttd))") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = strategy_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = strategy_colors) +
  
  # Expand the upper limits of the Y axis so the custom brackets fit perfectly
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(min(sim_results_processed$nxttd), max(selected_comparisons$y.position) + (y_step / 2))) +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
print(nttd_plot)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, supplement, "tte_mnt.png"), plot = nttd_plot, dpi = dpi, width = fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)


panel <- arrangeGrob(plot_absolute, nttd_plot, layout_matrix = rbind(c(1, 1, 2)), ncol = 3)
ggsave(paste0(manuscript_root, "tte_effectiveness_multipanel.png"), plot = panel, dpi = dpi, width = fig_width, height = fig_height, units = "cm", limitsize = FALSE)


strategy_medians <- sim_results_processed %>%
  group_by(Strategy) %>%
  summarise(
    Min_nxttd    = min(nxttd, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1_nxttd     = quantile(nxttd, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), # 25th Percentile
    Median_nxttd = median(nxttd, na.rm = TRUE),        # 50th Percentile
    Q3_nxttd     = quantile(nxttd, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), # 75th Percentile
    Max_nxttd    = max(nxttd, na.rm = TRUE),
    Sample_Size  = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Arrange from lowest footprint (most efficient) to highest
  arrange(Median_nxttd)

# Print the structured summary table to the console
print(strategy_medians)
```
